inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made it harder to revoke pre-arrest bail, saying that missing stolen articles and serious allegations aren’t enough without clear proof that liberty was misused or circumstances changed. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed a plea to cancel bail in a house case. That may be framed as a safeguard, but it also creates a convenient shield: if evidence is hard to produce or kept out of sight, the accused can remain protected while the public is told the rules were followed.
